harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with the sticky bit (mode 1777, root:root), which allows any user to write files while preventing users from deleting files owned by others. Verified the protection with two test users, cleaned up test artifacts, then performed the mandatory single-node restart protocol on node1 (baseline capture, safe reboot, boot_id change verification, post-restart re-verification of /srv/drop permissions and sticky-bit enforcement).
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop with mkdir + chmod 1777 via sudo
Verified ownership/permissions (1777, drwxrwxrwt, owner root:root)
Created two test users (dropuser1, dropuser2) to validate sticky-bit behavior
Confirmed dropuser2 could NOT delete dropuser1's file (Operation not permitted), but could create its own file
Confirmed dropuser1 could delete its own file
Cleaned up test files and test users, leaving /srv/drop empty and owned by root
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and uptime, and /srv/drop state
Issued sudo shutdown -r now in background to allow ack to return before disconnection
Confirmed connection loss (timeout) proving the reboot was in progress
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified new boot_id and new uptime start time, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions/ownership persisted post-restart
Re-verified sticky-bit protection still functions post-restart using fresh test users, then cleaned them up

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as shared writable directory with sticky bit set
evidence.summary: mkdir + chmod 1777 succeeded; stat shows mode 1777, drwxrwxrwt, owner=root group=root

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement) - pre-restart
evidence.summary: Created dropuser1/dropuser2; dropuser1 wrote file1.txt; dropuser2's rm attempt failed with 'Operation not permitted'; dropuser2 could write its own file2.txt; dropuser1 could delete its own file1.txt

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of verification artifacts before finishing
evidence.summary: Removed leftover test file and deleted both test users; /srv/drop left empty with correct 1777 permissions
Captured boot_id 33b0e84c-4dd1-406a-8f89-2e8ceca97bd6, uptime since 2026-08-26 10:34:49, and /srv/drop mode 1777
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned REBOOT_ACK immediately before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Proof node actually went down / restart in progress
evidence.summary: Subsequent exec attempt timed out connecting to node1, confirming it was rebooting

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving restart completed
evidence.summary: New boot_id 3934e984-9f6c-4a67-837c-c293563f904a (different from baseline) and new uptime start 2026-09-29 10:40:15

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and data
evidence.summary: stat confirms /srv/drop still mode 1777, owner root:root, empty as left before restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart re-verification that sticky-bit protection still functions
evidence.summary: New test users verifyuser1/verifyuser2 confirm verifyuser2 cannot delete verifyuser1's file post-restart; cleanup performed
